abstract: Perineuronal nets (PNN) is the specialized extracellular matrix that enwraps the soma and proximal dendrites of neurons in particular interneurons. During neural development, PNN expression marks the closure of the critical period of visual cortical development. The roles of PNN in the adult brain and how its expression is regulated remain less understood. Here we show that enriched environment (EE) increases PNN in the prefrontal cortex (PFC) in adult mice with improved cognitive functions. Analysis of snRNA-seq data of EE and control PFC identified the neuregulin1 (NRG1)/ErbB4 signaling as the pathway to regulate PNN expression. Ablation of ErbB4 or acute chemical genetic inhibition of its kinase activity reduced PNN and impaired cognitive function and prevented the promotion effect of EE. The expression of PNN and the core component aggrecan (ACAN) was increased in cultured interneurons stimulated with NRG1. ACAN mutation abolished PNN, weakened excitatory inputs and intrinsic excitability of ErbB4+ interneurons, and impaired cognitive functions. ACAN could undergo liquid-liquid phase separation to form condensates alone or together with other proteoglycans of the PNN. Finally, we demonstrate that restoring ACAN could ameliorate PNN and cognitive deficits in ErbB4 mutant mice. These results suggest that EE may improve cognitive functions by enhancing NRG1/ErbB4 signaling to increase PNN levels, identifying a signaling pathway critical to PNN homeostasis in adult animals
